title: The Knees Keep Their Own Calendar
body: Rain used to be atmosphere. Now it is a medical opinion. A doctor in Midtown says the body is a ledger that does not forgive late entries.

choices.text: Slow the year. Pay the clinic.

outcomes.title: A softer walk
outcomes.body: You buy time the way you used to buy turf. The name can wait one night.

choices.text: Push through. The city does not sit.

outcomes.title: Pride in the joints
outcomes.body: You make the meeting. The body files a complaint you will read later.

outcomes.title: A wet sidewalk
outcomes.body: The year takes a piece of you. Someone helps you up who should not know your name.

title: Ink for After You
body: A lawyer wants the chair written down while you can still hold a pen. The empty chair in the Hall is not a metaphor tonight.

choices.text: Write the heir. Say it out loud.

outcomes.title: A named tomorrow
outcomes.body: The paper is not kindness. It is a fence. The family sleeps a little less afraid.

choices.text: Wait. Superstition is a kind of law.

outcomes.title: An unwritten chair
outcomes.body: You keep the power and the fog. Someone will fight over the fog later.
outcomes.log: Refused to draft a late will.

title: A Small Voice at the Books
body: A child in the name asks what you did for a living. The honest answer would end the evening. The kind answer would start a lie you have to keep.

choices.text: Tell the kind version.

outcomes.title: A softer myth
outcomes.body: They hear about rain and work. You hear the chair creak. Bond holds.

choices.text: Tell enough truth to stain the year.

outcomes.title: A heavier myth
outcomes.body: They will not sleep the same. The name gets an heir who knows the weather.

title: A House Buries Someone
body: A rival family puts a body in the rain and expects flowers. Missing it is a statement. Attending is another. Cass will count the chairs.

choices.text: Go. Stand in the back. Mean it.

outcomes.title: Shared weather
outcomes.body: You do not speak. You are seen. Hostility cools because grief is a kind of truce.

choices.text: Send flowers. Stay home.

outcomes.title: A polite absence
outcomes.body: The card is perfect. The empty chair is louder than the card.
outcomes.log: Sent flowers to a rival funeral.

title: The Chair Creaks When You Stand
body: You have sat long enough that standing is news. Crew watch how you rise. Heirs watch harder.

choices.text: Hold the year. Smile like it does not hurt.

outcomes.title: Still in the chair
outcomes.body: They believe you, mostly. The books stay yours. The body files a memo.

choices.text: Let an heir sit beside you.

outcomes.title: A shared hour
outcomes.body: Power looks like trust. Trust looks like a rehearsal for your absence.
outcomes.log: Shared the late chair for an hour.

title: A Walk Through Old Quarter
body: The bricks remember your first year better than the new glass does. Someone who knew you at eighteen is selling coffee like it is a truce.

choices.text: Sit. Buy the coffee. Hear the decade.

outcomes.title: A cheap hour
outcomes.body: You learn who died of ordinary years. The city feels smaller and more expensive.
outcomes.log: Walked Old Quarter in a late year.

choices.text: Stay in the car. Keep the year moving.

outcomes.title: A faster rain
outcomes.body: You miss the names. You keep the schedule. That is how bosses get old.

title: The Last Honest Audit
body: A hand you trust says the take is lying. Late life is when loyalty and arithmetic finally meet in a room without windows.

choices.text: Cut the leak. Pay the honest ones.

outcomes.title: A cleaner book
outcomes.body: Someone walks. The numbers sit up. The table is smaller and true.
outcomes.log: Cut a late-life leak in the books.

choices.text: Forgive the leak. Keep the peace.

outcomes.title: A softer table
outcomes.body: You buy loyalty with blindness. It works until it does not.

title: Fog on the Last Crane
body: The docks look like 1998 if you squint. A crate sits unclaimed again. You are old enough to know it is never unclaimed.

choices.text: Leave it. You have stolen enough years.

outcomes.title: A crate that stays
outcomes.body: Someone younger will take the lesson. You take the walk home.
outcomes.log: Left a late-life crate on the docks.

choices.text: Open it. Old habits pay rent.

outcomes.title: A last easy night
outcomes.body: Cash, still. Heat, still. You laugh like eighteen and feel like a receipt.
outcomes.log: Opened a late crate on the docks.

outcomes.title: Vale's weather
outcomes.body: The crate was a story someone wanted you to finish. The year gets louder.

title: A Stone That Wants a Name
body: A mason in Old Quarter offers to cut the dynasty into granite while you can still argue the spelling. Superstition again. Also advertising.

choices.text: Cut the name. Pay for forever.

outcomes.title: Granite weather
outcomes.body: The stone will outlast the heat. Tourists will not know what it cost.
outcomes.log: Cut the name into Old Quarter stone.

choices.text: Let the hall be enough.

outcomes.title: No stone yet
outcomes.body: You refuse the grave's first draft. The rain approves, or does not care.

title: The Doctor Uses Your First Name
body: That is never a good sign. They want a slower life. The city wants the old one. You are the only voter.

choices.text: Obey. Lose a little empire.

outcomes.title: A smaller year
outcomes.body: You cancel a night that would have paid. The body sends a thank-you you cannot cash.

choices.text: Ignore it. The chair is not a bed.

outcomes.title: The old speed
outcomes.body: You keep the schedule. The doctor writes a note you will not read until it is too late to argue.
